title: First Reading, Second Reading
content: Jan Verhas (1834-1896)The LionIn a painting, you've just got just one image to tell the story. But you can design it so that the viewer begins to receive one impression, and then switch to a different impression after a moment or two. This is called the first reading and the second reading.In this picture, I'm aware of myself reacting that way as I decode the image over the first two seconds. "There's a lady with kid reaching up....The kid is scared...Oh! There's a crouching lion....how did he get in that house?....Oh, I see, it's a lion rug, and her little brother is under it, pulling a prank."To carry off this narrative device, Belgian realist painterJan Verhashad to make sure the viewer recognized the snarling lion before the boy's face.----Related post: "Invite and Delight"
